mechanism: Xelafaslatide, formerly ONL1204 Ophthalmic Solution, is an investigational first-in-class small peptide Fas inhibitor designed to block Fas-mediated retinal-cell death and protect key retinal cells, including photoreceptors, in geographic atrophy associated with dry AMD.
development_status: ClinicalTrials.gov lists GALAXY (NCT06659445) as a recruiting Phase 2 multicenter, randomized, double-masked, sham-controlled, reference-arm study of intravitreal ONL1204 in geographic atrophy associated with AMD. Estimated enrollment is 324, actual study start was 2025-10-28, estimated primary completion is November 2028, estimated study completion is November 2028, and no results are posted. Trial arms include ONL1204 100 mcg every 12 weeks, ONL1204 200 mcg every 12 weeks, ONL1204 200 mcg every 24 weeks, sham every 12 or 24 weeks, and a U.S.-only avacincaptad pegol reference arm.
expected_launch_window: 2031-2033 if Phase 2 is positive and subsequent pivotal development supports filing
clinical_summary: ONL1204 is differentiated from approved GA complement inhibitors by its proposed Fas-mediated neuroprotection mechanism and less frequent trial dosing every 12 or 24 weeks. The Phase 2 GALAXY primary endpoint is GA lesion area from enrollment through 48 weeks, with safety endpoints including new active exudative macular neovascularization and ETDRS BCVA loss. The completed Phase 1b GA study enrolled 28 patients, was primarily safety-focused, and reported no major safety findings or dose-limiting toxicities in the dose-escalation/open-label component; all ophthalmic adverse events in the randomized component were mild or moderate. Phase 1b efficacy signals were numerical rather than definitive, including slower GA lesion growth in the 200 mcg group versus sham with a mean difference of -0.524 mm2 and P = 0.202.
safety_summary: Early GA Phase 1b data reported ONL1204 was generally safe and well tolerated, with no major safety findings or dose-limiting toxicities in the dose-escalation component and only mild or moderate ophthalmic adverse events in the randomized component. The Phase 2 GALAXY trial is actively assessing ocular safety, including new active exudative macular neovascularization and ETDRS BCVA loss. Because ONL1204 is administered by intravitreal injection, payer management should anticipate class-procedure risks such as endophthalmitis, retinal detachment, neovascular AMD, intraocular inflammation, and intraocular pressure elevation seen in approved intravitreal GA therapies.
management_tools: Medical-benefit prior authorization for intravitreal administration
Diagnosis confirmation of geographic atrophy secondary to AMD
Age criterion aligned to trial population and any final label
Baseline documentation of GA lesion area by fundus autofluorescence or OCT-supported imaging
Exclusion for GA due to non-AMD causes unless supported by final label
Safety screen for active ocular or periocular infection and active intraocular inflammation before injection
Dose and frequency limit aligned to final FDA label; draft limits can model every 12-week or every 24-week ONL1204 dosing
No concurrent use with another GA intravitreal complement inhibitor unless supported by evidence or label
Continuation criteria requiring stable or reduced GA lesion growth, stabilization of vision-loss rate, or other label-supported clinical benefit
evidence_gaps: No Phase 2 efficacy or safety results are available for NCT06659445.
Phase 1b GA efficacy findings are small-sample and numerical; the 200 mcg comparison versus sham was not statistically significant.
No public Phase 3 plan, regulatory filing plan, FDA breakthrough designation, or launch timing was found for GA.

No public ONL1204 price is available; annual cost uses approved intravitreal GA therapies as analogs and assumes lower-frequency ONL1204 dosing is not offset by materially higher per-injection pricing.

ClinicalTrials.gov lists a 48-week primary endpoint, while ONL's clinical-trials page describes dosing every 12 or 24 weeks for 72 weeks; final development protocol timing should be rechecked as the trial matures.

sources.title: Study to Evaluate Efficacy and Safety of ONL1204 in Patients With GA Associated With AMD
supports: Official title is a Phase 2 multicenter, randomized, double-masked, sham-controlled, reference-arm study of ONL1204 in patients with geographic atrophy associated with AMD.
Sponsor is ONL Therapeutics; conditions are geographic atrophy and age-related macular degeneration.
Overall status is recruiting; actual start was 2025-10-28; estimated primary completion and study completion are November 2028.
Estimated enrollment is 324 and ClinicalTrials.gov hasResults is false.

Arms include ONL1204 100 mcg every 12 weeks, ONL1204 200 mcg every 12 weeks, ONL1204 200 mcg every 24 weeks, sham every 12 weeks, sham every 24 weeks, and a U.S.-only avacincaptad pegol active comparator arm.
Primary endpoint is GA lesion area from enrollment to end of treatment at 48 weeks.
Secondary safety endpoints include incidence of new active exudative macular neovascularization in the study eye and incidence of ETDRS best-corrected visual acuity loss.

Eligibility includes age 55 years or older, BCVA at least 24 ETDRS letters in the study eye, non-foveal GA associated with AMD, and exclusion of active ocular/periocular infection, active intraocular inflammation, current systemic complement inhibitors, and GA due to non-AMD causes.

sources.title: ONL Therapeutics Announces Randomization of First Patient in Global Phase 2 GALAXY Trial of Xelafaslatide (ONL1204) in Patients with Geographic Atrophy (GA) Associated with Dry AMD
supports: ONL announced the first participant randomized in the Phase 2 GALAXY trial.
GALAXY is designed to evaluate efficacy and safety of xelafaslatide, formerly ONL1204, in GA associated with dry AMD.
Xelafaslatide is the nonproprietary name for ONL1204 Ophthalmic Solution following WHO and USAN approval.
ONL describes xelafaslatide as an investigational first-in-class small molecule Fas inhibitor designed to protect key retinal cells, including photoreceptors.
ONL highlighted the novel Fas pathway and dosing every three to six months as potential differentiators versus current GA therapies.

sources.title: Clinical Trials - ONL Therapeutics
supports: ONL lists NCT06659445 as an active Phase 2 study in dry AMD/GA.
The company states the Phase 2 study collects efficacy and safety information across three experimental arms, including two ONL1204 dose levels and two dosing frequencies.
ONL lists intravitreal ONL1204 dosing every 12 weeks or 24 weeks for 72 weeks.
ONL lists dose levels of 100 mcg (50 mcL) and 200 mcg (100 mcL).
ONL lists the completed Phase 1b GA study, NCT04744662, and states ONL1204 was generally safe and well tolerated with efficacy signals after six months.

sources.title: ONL1204 Ophthalmic Solution in Patients With Geographic Atrophy Associated With Age-related Macular Degeneration
supports: Completed Phase 1b multicenter randomized controlled multidose study of ONL1204 in GA associated with AMD.
Sponsor was ONL Therapeutics; actual enrollment was 28.
Actual start was 2021-07-08; actual primary completion and study completion were 2024-02-29.
The study evaluated safety and tolerability of intravitreal ONL1204 in GA associated with AMD.
Primary safety-related measures included best corrected visual acuity, intraocular pressure, and slit-lamp biomicroscopy up to 48 weeks.
ClinicalTrials.gov hasResults is false.

sources.title: ONL1204 for the Treatment of Geographic Atrophy: Phase Ib Study Evaluating Safety, Tolerability, and Efficacy
supports: Peer-reviewed Phase 1b GA study evaluated ONL1204, a small peptide inhibitor of the fragment apoptosis stimulator receptor.
Dose-escalation/open-label patients received single intravitreal ONL1204 doses of 50 mcg, 100 mcg, or 200 mcg and were followed for 24 weeks.
Randomized natural-history/treatment component assigned patients to 50 mcg ONL1204, 200 mcg ONL1204, or sham after a 24-week natural-history phase; two injections were administered 12 weeks apart.
Six patients enrolled in the dose-escalation/open-label component and 22 patients enrolled in the natural-history/treatment component.
All dose-escalation/open-label patients completed the study with no major safety findings or dose-limiting toxicities.
Seventeen patients were randomized in the natural-history/treatment component and 15 completed the study; all ophthalmic adverse events were mild or moderate.
The 200 mcg ONL1204 group had numerically slower GA lesion growth versus sham in the treatment phase with mean difference -0.524 mm2, standard error 0.39, and P = 0.202.
The publication concluded ONL1204 was safe and well tolerated at all evaluated doses and supported further evaluation in GA.

sources.title: ONL Therapeutics Announces Publication of Data from Phase 1b Study of Xelafaslatide in Geographic Atrophy
supports: ONL announced publication of Phase 1b xelafaslatide data in Ophthalmology Science.
ONL stated xelafaslatide was generally safe and well tolerated in Phase 1b GA.
ONL stated additional assessments showed efficacy signals after six months with treated eyes slowing GA lesion growth compared with untreated eyes.
ONL described xelafaslatide as an investigational first-in-class small molecule Fas inhibitor designed to protect key retinal cells from cell death.
ONL stated later-stage development includes Phase 2 NCT06659445 for GA associated with AMD.

sources.title: DailyMed: IZERVAY (avacincaptad pegol intravitreal solution)
supports: IZERVAY is indicated for treatment of geographic atrophy secondary to AMD.
Recommended dose is 2 mg by intravitreal injection to each affected eye once monthly, approximately every 28 days plus or minus 7 days.
Warnings include endophthalmitis and retinal detachments, neovascular AMD, and increased intraocular pressure.
Common adverse reactions include conjunctival hemorrhage 13%, increased IOP 9%, blurred vision 8%, and neovascular AMD 7%.
Each vial should only be used for treatment of a single eye.

sources.title: DailyMed: SYFOVRE (pegcetacoplan injection)
supports: SYFOVRE is indicated for treatment of geographic atrophy secondary to AMD.
Recommended dose is 15 mg by intravitreal injection to each affected eye once every 25 to 60 days.
Warnings include endophthalmitis and retinal detachments, retinal vasculitis and/or retinal vascular occlusion, neovascular AMD, intraocular inflammation, and increased intraocular pressure.
Common adverse reactions include ocular discomfort, neovascular AMD, vitreous floaters, and conjunctival hemorrhage.
Each vial contains overfill to allow administration of a single 0.1 mL dose containing 15 mg of SYFOVRE.

sources.title: IZERVAY Pricing Microsite
supports: Astellas lists the IZERVAY list price as $2,100 per month.
The site defines one month as approximately 28 days plus or minus 7 days.
The pricing page states actual patient cost depends on insurance coverage and other factors.
The list-price information is based on AnalySource exported 2024-08-06.

sources.title: Syfovre Prices, Coupons, Copay Cards and Patient Assistance
supports: Drugs.com lists Syfovre 150 mg/mL intravitreal solution from $2,299.86 for 0.1 mL.
The listed price range for 0.1 mL is $2,299.86 to $2,414.45.
The page notes Syfovre is available as a brand-name drug only and no generic version is available.
The page cautions that pricing ranges may vary and consumers normally should expect the lower price.

sources.title: Ophthalmology - Syfovre Drug Coverage Policy
supports: Cigna requires prior authorization for Syfovre prescription benefit coverage.
Coverage for FDA-approved GA requires GA secondary to AMD, BCVA of 24 ETDRS letters or better or 20/320 or better by Snellen, and administration by or under supervision of an ophthalmologist.
Cigna dose criteria require 15 mg intravitreal injection for each treated eye and dosing not more frequent than once every 25 days per treated eye.
Cigna considers concomitant use with Izervay not medically necessary because no data support concomitant use.

sources.title: Avacincaptad Pegol (Izervay) - Medical Clinical Policy Bulletin
supports: Aetna states Izervay requires precertification in applicable commercial plan designs.
Aetna commercial policy requires ophthalmologist prescribing or consultation.
Aetna considers Izervay medically necessary for GA secondary to AMD and considers other indications experimental, investigational, or unproven.

Continuation requires demonstrated positive clinical response, such as improvement or maintenance in BCVA or visual field, or a reduction in the rate of vision decline or risk of more severe vision loss.
Aetna states Izervay is medically necessary only after contraindication, intolerance, or ineffective response to lower-cost Syfovre because reliable evidence of superiority is lacking.

expected_launch_window.value: 2031-2033 if Phase 2 is positive and subsequent pivotal development supports filing
expected_launch_window.method: Used NCT06659445 estimated primary completion in November 2028, current Phase 2 status, absence of Phase 3 or filing guidance, and typical need for pivotal trials before approval of a new GA therapy.
expected_launch_window.explanation: A launch before 2031 appears unlikely because GALAXY is still recruiting and is Phase 2; approval would likely require positive Phase 2 data, pivotal development, filing, and FDA review.

annual_cost_range.method: Used approved GA intravitreal product prices as per-injection analogs: low assumes IZERVAY list price $2,100 per injection and ONL1204 every 24 weeks, or two injections per treated eye per year; high assumes Syfovre upper listed price $2,414.45 per injection and ONL1204 every 12 weeks, or four injections per treated eye per year. Rounded $2,100 x 2 = $4,200 and $2,414.45 x 4 = $9,657.80 to $9,658.
annual_cost_range.explanation: The estimate is a gross drug-only analog for one treated eye and excludes rebates, discounts, administration fees, bilateral treatment, imaging, visits, wastage, or any ONL launch-price premium or discount.

clinical_differentiation.method: Balanced novel Fas-mediated neuroprotection, every-12-week or every-24-week trial dosing, and supportive Phase 1b safety/numerical lesion-growth signals against lack of Phase 2 efficacy results and small non-significant Phase 1b efficacy data.
clinical_differentiation.explanation: ONL1204 could be meaningfully differentiated if Phase 2 confirms efficacy with lower injection burden, but current evidence remains early and not yet registration-grade.

budget_impact.method: Assessed analog per-eye annual drug cost of about $4.2k to $9.7k under trial dosing, large Medicare-relevant GA population, medical-benefit intravitreal administration, and existing payer controls for approved GA therapies.
budget_impact.explanation: Lower dosing frequency could moderate per-patient annual drug spend versus monthly or every-other-month GA therapies, but GA prevalence, bilateral treatment potential, administration costs, and uncertain launch pricing keep budget impact material.

disruption_risk.method: Rated from early Phase 2 status and long launch horizon, offset by novel non-complement mechanism, potential dosing advantage, and established payer sensitivity to GA therapy cost and utilization controls.
disruption_risk.explanation: The asset is not near launch, but positive Phase 2 data could create meaningful formulary and policy work because ONL1204 would enter a costly intravitreal GA category with differentiated mechanism and dosing.

recommended_action.method: Recommended action reflects recruiting Phase 2 status, primary completion not expected until November 2028, no posted Phase 2 results, and no public Phase 3 or filing timeline.
recommended_action.explanation: Monitor GALAXY enrollment, protocol updates, Phase 2 data, and any pivotal-study plans; active formulary planning can wait until efficacy and pricing assumptions are less speculative.

quality_flags: No posted ClinicalTrials.gov results for NCT06659445.
Current evidence is Phase 2 recruiting plus small Phase 1b GA data; no registration-enabling efficacy package is public.
Annual cost estimate is analog-derived from approved intravitreal GA therapies and ONL1204 trial dosing, not from an ONL price.
Per-eye cost estimate excludes administration fees, imaging/monitoring costs, bilateral treatment, rebates, discounts, and future launch-pricing strategy.
ClinicalTrials.gov uses the intervention spelling 'Opthalmic solution' in arm labels; packet normalizes the asset name to ONL1204 Ophthalmic Solution.
ClinicalTrials.gov and ONL's clinical-trials page differ on visible treatment-duration framing, with CT.gov listing a 48-week primary endpoint and ONL describing dosing for 72 weeks.
